title: kv-cache-spillover-and-fragmentation-mitigation-with-paging-allocator
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add adaptive spillover paging and per-shard allocator to reduce KV cache fragmentation and OOMs; introduces new metrics and a feature flag. No public API changes.
description: Motivation: Under high-concurrency workloads with long-lived context windows we observed growing memory fragmentation in the KV store that increases tail latency and leads to OOMs on memory-constrained runners. This PR implements a multi-pronged approach: 1) a per-shard memory arena/allocator to avoid cross-shard fragmentation, 2) a size-aware LRU eviction policy, and 3) a spillover paging layer that moves cold KV segments to a compressed local spill store (NVMe) under pressure. Design summary: - Per-shard arenas: each KV shard gets a slab/buddy-style arena to keep allocation lifetimes co-located and reduce external fragmentation. Arena sizes adapt to workload footprints. - Size-aware eviction: eviction heuristics include both recency and compressed-on-disk size to avoid thrashing due to large entries. - Spillover paging: on eviction when total resident memory exceeds adaptive thresholds, cold entries are serialized to a compressed spill store. The spill store is page-oriented (4MB pages) and uses an append-only file with a background compactor to reclaim free pages. - Adaptive thresholds: thresholds are tuned using allocation rate and recent GC/eviction rates; the runtime backs off aggressive batching if spill IO increases above a configured target to avoid latency spikes. - Metrics and observability: new metrics exported (kv_cache.heap_frag_ratio, kv_cache.spill_io_ops, kv_cache.spill_store_bytes, kv_cache.evictions_by_policy, kv_cache.eviction_latency_ms) and debug endpoints to inspect per-shard arena usage. Implementation notes: - Core allocator in src/runtime/kv_cache/allocator.rs implements per-shard arenas, a small-bins fast-path for tiny KV entries, and a buddy fallback for larger allocations. - Eviction logic moved to src/runtime/kv_cache/eviction.rs; eviction now consults size and recency and considers spill eligibility based on configured TTL and pinned flags. - Spill store implemented in src/runtime/kv_cache/spill_store.rs with an async IO worker pool and a compacting pass triggered when free page ratio falls below 20%. - Integration with continuous batching: batching pipeline was updated to consult a new runtime.kv.allow_spill config so hot requests avoid spill-induced I/O. - Feature flag & rollout: runtime.kv.spillover is gated behind a feature flag; enabled by default for Dedicated runners in the rollout plan, opt-in for hosted for the first month. Tests & benchmarks: - Unit tests added for arena allocation edge cases, compaction correctness, and eviction policy invariants. - Integration tests simulate high fragmentation patterns and verify zero OOMs for workloads that previously tripped memory limits. - Microbench: on a 64-GPU Dedicated pool synthetic workload (mix of long and short contexts) we observe: 60% reduction in observed OOM incidents, 14% improvement in p99 token latency under memory pressure, and 8-12% throughput improvement at steady state due to less GC-induced stalls. Backwards compatibility & migration: no public API changes. Disk-based spill files are incompatible across runtime minor versions; the rollout includes a migration window where older spill files are ignored and re-populated. Operational notes: - New alerts: kv_cache.heap_frag_ratio > 0.45 sustained for 5m, kv_cache.spill_io_ops > 100/s sustained triggers pager-backpressure alert. - Default config tuned conservatively; ops can lower spill thresholds for aggressive memory reclamation. Related work: previous PRs that added per-shard metrics and earlier eviction heuristics (ENG-4982) and the profiler changes (ENG-5210). Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Benchmarks recorded - [x] Feature-flagged rollout plan - [x] Observability dashboards updated

review_comments: Diego Marquez: Can you clarify how the compactor avoids long pauses? if it scans the whole file it may spike tail latency.

Asha Patel: The compactor is background and rate-limited; it compacts in 4MB page chunks and yields between passes. We also bound the max work per second configurable via runtime.kv.compactor.max_bytes_per_sec.
Tomás Rivera: We saw a flaky integration test on CI related to delayed spill writes; suggest adding deterministic flushing in tests.
Asha Patel: Added deterministic flush hooks and made the test wait on a flush future; CI rerun passed.
Maya Singh: Can the eviction policy be tuned per-tenant? Some customers store very large embeddings and we'd prefer size-first eviction.
Asha Patel: Added runtime.kv.eviction.policy which supports 'recency','size','hybrid' and documented recommended settings in docs/ops/kv_spillover.md.
merge_commit_message:
kv: reduce fragmentation and add spillover paging + per-shard allocator (ENG-5421)

Adds adaptive spillover to NVMe, size-aware eviction, and observability. Feature-flagged rollout for Dedicated.
notes_for_ops: Enable runtime.kv.spillover in Dedicated and monitor kv_cache.heap_frag_ratio and kv_cache.spill_io_ops. Default compactor rate is conservative; increase only after load testing.
changelog_entry: Runtime: Improve KV cache memory management with spillover paging and per-shard allocator. Reduces OOMs and tail latency under memory pressure. (ENG-5421)
incident_reference: This PR was prioritized after a Support spike (SUP-1203) where customers on Dedicated saw OOMs under mixed-context workloads. The changes address root causes related to fragmentation and unbounded resident memory growth.
